source_preparation: LAUREL NUTRILAB lacto-vegetarian trial soup: older-adult functional-compensation comparison

citation.title: Daily Supplementation with Protein-Enriched Lacto-Vegetarian Soups and Muscle Health in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
citation.authors: Kao SL, Wang JH, Lai HY, Hsiao FY, Chen LK, Loh CH.
citation.journal: The Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging 29(3):100477 (2025)

preparation.exposure: One pack ingested daily for 12 weeks, providing 24–30 g protein; frozen delivery or self-collection.
preparation.protein_sources_as_current_registry: May come from soy, beans or milk products.
preparation.wording_limit: Methods 2.3 initially describes 24–30 grams of protein-enriched soups; abstract, allocation paragraph and surrounding Methods specify protein per serving. Total soup mass is not recovered.
preparation.comparator: Usual diet/healthy-aging education without nutritional supplementation; no energy/protein/ingredient matched placebo.
preparation.lifestyle: No assigned exercise; both groups asked to maintain usual diet/lifestyle and avoid added supplements or intervention programs.
preparation.attribution_limit: Whole preparation versus education/usual diet; cannot isolate protein from energy, other ingredients, expectations or behavior.

design_population.design: Open-label parallel randomized trial; computer-generated blocks of 4, stratified by age and sex, independent allocator, sealed envelopes opened after baseline assessment.
design_population.recruitment_setting: Hualien Tzu Chi Hospital and community channels, Taiwan

withdrawals.control_reason: Fall/lower-limb fracture and subsequent lifestyle change

design_population.eligibility: Age ≥65, MNA-SF ≤11, SARC-F ≥4 or SARC-CalF ≥11, willingness/ability to consent; exclude intolerance, serious/uncontrolled disease including cirrhosis/eGFR<30, relevant malignancy and major sensory impairment. Current registry gives further exclusions.
design_population.population_limit: Selected older adults at nutritional/sarcopenia risk, not all vegetarians or all confirmed sarcopenia diagnoses; no MVA population.
design_population.masking: None in current registry; main open-label; no verified outcome-assessor masking.
design_population.missingness: Three randomized withdrawals excluded; no ITT definition, imputation or sensitivity analysis reported. Table 2 chair-rise n=46 intervention/48 control versus most rows48/49. Table 3 endpoint-specific denominators absent.

paper_primary_domains: Functional assessments including SARC-F, SARC-CalF, MNA-SF, MMSE, GDS-15
hierarchy_and_statistics.paper_secondary: Cardiometabolic/inflammatory biomarkers; additional renal/hepatic/electrolyte/vitamin measures reported.
hierarchy_and_statistics.within_group_test: Paired t test; Table2 mean ± SD.
hierarchy_and_statistics.between_group_baseline_tests: Student t test/chi-square as described; not a new balance test here.
hierarchy_and_statistics.GEE_reported_comparative_scope: Author-reported intervention-versus-control GEE endpoint comparison at 12 weeks, based on Table 3 title and Results/Discussion. Exact group/reference/time coding and adjustment unspecified; do not label as independently verified adjusted change or interaction.
hierarchy_and_statistics.GEE_title: The impacts of protein-enriched lacto-vegetarian soups on outcomes at 12th week using generalized estimating equations.
hierarchy_and_statistics.multiplicity: No correction across multiple primary domains, components and numerous laboratory outcomes described. Nominal two-sided P<.05.

functional_findings.interpretation: Raw trajectories and initial functional separation are distinct from author-reported GEE betas. Do not infer a wrong model from their mismatch, reconstruct an adjusted change effect, or erase comparative endpoint findings.
functional_findings.test_definitions: SPPB balance/chair and 4-m walking in Methods; separate table/current-registry walk uses 6 m. Grip is best of 3 dominant-hand Smedley measurements. Preserve labels.
functional_findings.component_dependency: Chair-rise and composite SPPB are related outcomes, not independent replications.
functional_findings.ceiling_context: Intervention SPPB baseline 10.8/final 11.4 near upper score 12.

body_composition_reporting.abstract: Broad wording says no significant body-composition changes in intervention.
body_composition_reporting.main_within_group: Table 2/Results report intervention waist, hip, total body water and skeletal muscle mass increases; muscle mass 18.8 ±3.0 to 19.0 ±2.9 kg, P=.003.
body_composition_reporting.GEE: All Table3 body-composition coefficients nonpositive; muscle mass −0.32 kg (−1.49,0.86), P=.60; ASM 0.06 kg/m² (−0.21,0.34), P=.65.
body_composition_reporting.limit: Keep wording and test types separate; within-arm gain is not comparative gain, and comparative nonpositive result does not erase within-arm observation. BIA is not direct tissue renewal.

source_qualification.lab_findings: Within-arm changes in both groups; no Table3 cardiometabolic, inflammatory, renal, hepatic, electrolyte or vitamin coefficient is significant under its printed P. Do not convert lab nonpositives into renal/hepatic safety equivalence.

nutrient_rows.limits: Table 3 nutrient rows omit units, complete assessment details and baseline/final intake values. Not the soup nutrient label or demonstrated 24–30 g increase in total daily intake.

scientific_summary: The open-label randomized Taiwan trial tested one commercially described LAUREL NUTRILAB lacto-vegetarian soup daily, providing 24–30 g protein for 12 weeks, against usual diet/healthy-aging education without a supplement. One hundred adults aged at least 65 at nutritional and sarcopenia risk were randomized 50/50; 48 intervention/49 control participants were analyzed, with chair testing in 46/48. Table 3 and Results report comparative 12-week GEE coefficients favoring soup for SPPB (+0.83 points, 95% CI 0.15–1.51; P=.02) and chair-rise time (−2.25 seconds, −4.04 to −0.44; P=.01). These are reported intervention-versus-control endpoint positives; exact coding, baseline adjustment and change/interaction construction are unrecovered, so raw-change differences neither reconstruct nor invalidate the model. Grip (+0.37 kg; P=.76), six-metre walk (−0.65 seconds; P=.07) and all body-composition comparisons were nonsignificant. Within-arm mass gain is a separate observation. SARC-F and MNA-SF were nominally favorable; other functional and laboratory comparisons were nonsignificant. The recipe, ingredient proportions and current retail equivalent are unknown; registry protein sources may include soy, beans or milk. Unmatched food energy, open-label behavior, multiple outcomes, baseline differences and missingness prevent an isolated-protein conclusion. No severe adverse reactions were reported, without a graded comparative safety table; regimen withdrawals and a control fracture are retained. Current registry hierarchy differs from the paper, without verified original history. Industry–academic support is disclosed. This preparation adds useful functional comparative evidence without establishing generic soup/protein efficacy, MVA benefit, tissue renewal or superiority to the provisional nominees.
identity_limit: Automatic aliases are withheld. The source-specific trial label and supplier do not identify a unique recipe or equivalent catalog/retail product. Generic protein, soy, bean, milk, lacto-vegetarian soup and LAUREL alone must not inherit this result.
